gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in a Florida September (NREL PVWatts for Jacksonville: 49 kWh a month from a 400 W panel), the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2's single 200 W kit panel returns about 817 Wh a day against a fridge's 1.6 kWh a day, so the 2,028 Wh that APH Networks measured lasts about 2.6 days, while the 2×200 W kit ($300 more) about breaks even on clear days.
standout_why: Compared against backup-power.org (cited), EnergySage (cited) and ChatGPT's own answer; Good Housekeeping (cited) could not be fetched. backup-power.org already says 'One 200W panel doesn't cover that even on a good day' and 'Two panels get close in most of the country', using a generic 4.5 sun-hour example (200 × 4.5 × 0.86 ≈ 774 Wh) and a 1.6 kWh/day fridge, and it already lists the Elite 200 V2 + 2×200W kit. EnergySage only does Wh ÷ panel watts for ideal refill times and a 1,500 Wh/day fridge at 85% usable. ChatGPT says a 200 W panel gives 'roughly 500–1,000 Wh on a reasonably sunny day'. None of them gives a yield for the hurricane months in Florida, a measured usable Wh, or a per-kit count of outage days with the kit's own panel feeding the fridge. Those parts are new; the main conclusion is not.
decides: Confirms the Elite 200 V2 but points to the 2×200 W kit ($1,499, BLUETTI store) rather than the 1×200 W kit ($1,199) that ChatGPT and our page lead with. The extra $300 adds about 817 Wh a day of September sun in Florida. That turns a 2.6-day fridge run-down into about break-even on clear days (before charge-controller losses). The DELTA 2 Max kit with one 220 W panel runs down the same way as the 1×200 W BLUETTI kit.
